lead: A former textile village with a shopping street, squares, a festa major and the city's railway station.
text: Santa Maria de Sants was a municipality in its own right until 1897 and in the 19th century was a working-class neighbourhood of textile mills: the Vapor Vell, owned by the Güell family, was the first, and España Industrial, owned by the Muntadas family, was another of the big ones. Between 1850 and its incorporation into Barcelona the population multiplied fivefold. That past shows in its neighbourhood life: Carrer de Sants and Creu Coberta as shopping streets, squares where people gather and a festa major in August that fills the streets with decorations. The new Mercat de Sants opened in 2014, with 3,000 m² of retail space and a car park of 90 spaces. In November 2025 the City Council gave initial approval to the amendment to the general plan for the area around the Jardins de la Rambla de Sants and the Rambla de Badal, which sets aside 5,000 m² of land for public facilities and reduces the number of affected homes from 85 to 12; final approval rests with the Urban Planning Subcommittee.

Here you live close to everything: Sants station, with high-speed and commuter trains, and the Parc de l'Espanya Industrial are in the neighbourhood, and Montjuïc, Plaça d'Espanya and the Diagonal are a few minutes away. It was also the setting for milestones in social history, such as the 1918 Sants Congress, at which the CNT was reorganised. At 4,310 €/m², it has the highest sale price in Sants-Montjuïc. If you are selling, the average sale price is 11% above the Sants-Montjuïc average. Within the neighbourhood, the price of each flat depends on its condition, its floor and its building, so it is best to compare it with nearby sales rather than with the district average. If you are buying, an 80 m² flat costs about 345,000 € on average, and this is one of the most expensive neighbourhoods in Sants-Montjuïc (1st of 8 by price). If you are investing, the average rent (995 €/month) is in line with the district; before deciding, it is worth studying each deal with real figures for purchase, renovation and rental income.
housing: Buildings from the early and mid-20th century, with shops at street level.
